How to read this

Higher points allowed can indicate a favorable fantasy matchup, but this is a historical signal—not a future opponent projection.

What is measured?
All fantasy points scored by players at the selected position against each defense, divided by distinct team-game matchups in the available data.

The highly scientific trade analysis formula

For entertainment only. Each player's Raw Performance combines 60% season fantasy points/game, 30% last-three-games average, and 10% season-low points/game. VOR (Value Over Replacement) measures how much better a player performs than an estimated replacement at the same position. It equals the raw score minus the positional benchmark (negative when below replacement). The Positional Performance Index (PPI) equals raw performance ÷ positional benchmark × 100. A score of 100 represents replacement level. One-for-one trades compare PPI directly (minimum zero for team totals). For multi-player trades, each side starts at 100 and adds only positive index points above 100 for each player, so extra replacement-level players add no value. Replacement players are ranked by the same weighted score and must have at least three appearances. This is not a rest-of-season forecast and does not account for injuries, schedule, roster needs, keeper value, or the value of open roster spots. Replacement thresholds are estimates, not actual waiver availability. Weights have not been backtested.

Historical estimate · not a live projection
Select at least two players to compare.

How the weekly score works

40% season points per game + 60% last-three-game average = baseline. Multiply the baseline by a matchup factor: 1 + 0.25 × (opponent positional points allowed per game ÷ league positional average − 1), limited to 0.80–1.20. If no opponent or insufficient data, factor = 1.00. These are initial heuristic weights, not backtested forecasts. No live injury or schedule feed is connected.

Source: nflverse stats_player • regular season only • historical data • no live projections.
